title: Architecting Space Microdatacenters: A System-level Approach
problem: There is no principled cost-aware methodology for architecting server-based computing systems deployed on low Earth orbit (LEO) satellites (Space Microdatacenters, SuDC). Prior work proposes the concept but does not model Total Cost of Ownership (TCO) to guide hardware design decisions.
motivation: LEO-based Earth observation satellites generate massive onboard data; processing it in space reduces downlink bandwidth and latency, but no hardware architecture framework accounts for the unique cost structure (power-vs-mass-vs-monetary trade-offs) of space compute.
method: The authors build a TCO model for SuDC that decomposes costs into compute power, mass, monetary hardware cost, and communication. They perform a design space exploration over heterogeneous accelerator configurations (high FLOPs/W devices), collaborative compute constellations (EO satellites with onboard accelerators), monolithic vs. distributed architectures, and compute overprovisioning strategies. TCO sensitivity analysis reveals power dominates sublinearly; monetary cost and mass are secondary.
key_novelty: First TCO-driven architecture framework for space microdatacenters, showing that extreme heterogeneity (high FLOPs/W ASICs/NPUs) reduces TCO by 116x despite poor FLOPs/$ characteristics.
contributions: First cost-aware (TCO) architecture analysis and optimization framework for Space Microdatacenters (SuDC).
Demonstration that compute power is the dominant TCO driver and that high FLOPs/W heterogeneous designs reduce SuDC TCO by 116x.
Analysis showing collaborative compute constellations (compute-equipped EO satellites) further improve TCO by 1.31-1.74x.
Finding that distributed SuDC architecture reduces TCO by 10% over monolithic, and compute overprovisioning enables near-zero-cost availability and graceful degradation.

metrics.energy_or_tops_w: 116x TCO reduction with extreme heterogeneity (high FLOPs/W) vs. homogeneous baseline
metrics.other: 1.31-1.74x additional TCO improvement with collaborative constellations; 10% TCO reduction distributed vs. monolithic

limitations: The analysis relies on modeled TCO and does not include a physical SuDC prototype or real-world space deployment validation.
primary_theme: TCO-driven heterogeneous architecture for space-based computing
